name: Jollof Rice
adaptationNote: Use vegetable stock + smoked paprika to make it vegetarian — still smoky and tasty.
blurb: The beloved party rice of Nigeria and Ghana — smoky, tomato-rich, and always at the centre of celebrations, Sundays, and friendly debates about who makes it best.

ingredients.name: Long-grain parboiled rice
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less smoky absorption; grains break more easily — still tasty.

ingredients.name: Fresh tomatoes
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Slightly less fresh sweetness; add a pinch of sugar.

ingredients.name: Red bell peppers
ingredients.substitution: Tatashe if you can find it
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Tatashe gives the classic colour and mild heat.

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet
ingredients.substitution: Habanero or ½ tsp chilli flakes
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Similar heat; habanero is a touch fruitier.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Loses some depth; paprika brings back smokiness. Makes it vegetarian.

steps.text: Blend tomatoes, bell peppers, scotch bonnet and half an onion until smooth.
Fry sliced onion and tomato paste in oil until the paste darkens and tastes sweet.
steps.why: Frying off the raw edge of tomato paste is what gives party-style depth.

steps.text: Add the blended mix and simmer until thick and the oil rises to the top.
steps.why: Thickening now means fluffy, separate grains later — watery sauce makes soggy rice.

steps.text: Stir in stock, thyme, bay leaf and salt. Bring to a boil, then add rinsed rice.
Cover tightly with foil + lid and cook on low until rice is tender.
steps.why: Trapped steam does the cooking — resist peeking for the first 15 minutes.

name: Egusi Soup
adaptationNote: Swap smoked fish/meat for mushrooms to make it vegetarian — still savoury, less smoky depth.
blurb: A hearty melon-seed soup eaten across Nigeria — nutty, rich, and made for scooping with swallow. A Sunday staple in many homes.

ingredients.name: Ground egusi (melon seeds)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Close in texture; slightly milder and less nutty.

ingredients.name: Palm oil
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Loses the signature colour and earthy flavour — honest downgrade.

ingredients.name: Spinach or bitter leaf
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Chewier; simmer 5 minutes longer.

ingredients.name: Smoked mackerel
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Mushrooms keep it savoury but lose the smoky-fish depth.

steps.text: Mix ground egusi with a splash of water into a thick paste; set aside.
Heat palm oil, fry onion, then add stock and bring to a simmer.
Scoop in egusi paste in lumps and simmer without stirring.
steps.why: Leaving it alone lets the egusi set into lovely crumbs instead of mush.

steps.text: Stir gently, add fish, greens and seasoning. Simmer until greens are tender.

name: Fufu
adaptationNote: Naturally vegan — just serve with a vegetarian soup like mushroom egusi.
blurb: Soft, stretchy swallow pounded from cassava and plantain — the scoop you use for soups like egusi and groundnut stew. Eaten daily across Ghana, Nigeria and beyond.

ingredients.name: Cassava flour (or fufu flour)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less stretch, much easier — a fair trade on busy days.

steps.text: Bring water to a boil, then whisk in the flour a little at a time.
Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until smooth and stretchy.
steps.why: Elbow grease now is what gives fufu its pull — keep turning, don't stop.

steps.text: Wet your hands, shape into balls and serve warm with soup.

name: Waakye
adaptationNote: Skip egg/fish sides and load up beans + shito for a vegan plate.
blurb: Ghana's famous rice-and-beans, cooked with sorghum leaves for its brick-red colour. A classic street breakfast wrapped in banana leaves with all the extras.

ingredients.name: Black-eyed beans
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Softer; skip the pre-boil and shorten cooking by ~20 min.

ingredients.name: Dried sorghum (waakye) leaves
ingredients.substitution: 1 tsp baking soda for colour only
ingredients.substitutionImpact: You get a brownish tint, not the classic red — flavour mostly unchanged.

steps.text: Boil beans with sorghum leaves until almost tender.
Remove leaves, add rice, salt and water. Cover and cook on low.
steps.why: Beans need a head start or the rice turns to mush before they soften.

steps.text: Rest 10 minutes, fluff, and serve with extras (egg, shito, spaghetti).

name: Puff-Puff
adaptationNote: Naturally vegan — fry in fresh vegetable oil.
blurb: Golden, pillowy fried dough balls — the snack of every Nigerian party and street corner. Best eaten warm, standing up, with friends.

ingredients.name: Ground nutmeg
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less traditional warmth; still sweet and lovely.

steps.text: Mix everything into a thick batter. Cover and proof until doubled and bubbly.
steps.why: A full, bubbly rise is what makes them hollow-light instead of dense.

steps.text: Heat oil to 170–175°C. Scoop batter with oiled hands or a spoon.
Fry in batches, turning, until deep golden all over. Drain on paper.
steps.why: Crowding the pot drops the oil temperature and makes them greasy.

name: Groundnut Stew
adaptationNote: Swap chicken for sweet potato + chickpeas to make it vegetarian — add an extra spoon of peanut butter.
blurb: Known as mafé across Senegal and Mali — a comforting peanut stew, gently sweet and savoury, eaten with rice or fufu on family evenings.

ingredients.name: Natural peanut butter (no sugar)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Grainier texture, deeper roast flavour — very good.

ingredients.name: Chicken pieces
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Lighter but still hearty; add an extra spoon of peanut butter.

ingredients.name: Carrots & sweet potato
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Sweeter and softer — lovely, just watch the simmer time.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in oil; set aside.
Fry onion and tomato paste, then whisk in stock and peanut butter until smooth.
steps.why: Whisking bit by bit stops the peanut splitting later.

steps.text: Return chicken plus vegetables. Simmer until tender and oil glistens on top.

name: Thiéboudienne
adaptationNote: Swap fish for cauliflower steaks + chickpeas and use vegetable stock for a vegetarian pot — keep the tamarind, it carries the flavour.
blurb: Senegal's proud national dish — broken rice cooked in a rich tomato-tamarind broth with fish and root vegetables. Served communally, eaten with joy.

ingredients.name: Broken rice (or jasmine)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less traditional bite; jasmine soaks up the broth beautifully anyway.

ingredients.name: Firm white fish steaks
ingredients.substitution: Sea bass, grouper or red snapper
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Any firm fish holds together; avoid soft fillets that flake apart.

ingredients.name: Tamarind pulp
ingredients.substitution: Juice of 1 lime + 1 tsp extra tomato paste
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Brighter and less deep, but keeps the needed sour lift.

ingredients.name: Cassava, carrot & cabbage
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Softer and sweeter; still very good.

steps.text: Season fish, sear in oil until golden, and set aside.
steps.why: Searing first keeps the fish in one piece through the long simmer.

steps.text: Fry onion, tomato paste and tamarind in the same oil until deep red and sweet.
Add stock and root vegetables; simmer until just tender, then lift vegetables out.
steps.why: Cooking veg separately stops them collapsing while the rice finishes.

steps.text: Add rice to the broth, cover and steam on low until tender.
Return fish and vegetables to warm through, then serve from one big dish.

name: Chicken Yassa
adaptationNote: Use big mushrooms + extra onions instead of chicken for a vegetarian yassa — the lemon-mustard sauce is the star anyway.
blurb: Chicken marinated in lemon and mustard with a mountain of caramelised onions — sharp, savoury and comforting over rice. A Casamance classic.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less meaty but the tangy onion sauce still shines.

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Softer bite; add a squeeze more lemon.

ingredients.name: Lemons, juiced
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Sharper; use a little less.

steps.text: Marinate chicken with lemon, mustard, salt and half the onions for at least 1 hour (overnight is best).
steps.why: The acid tenderises and the mustard flavour soaks right in — do not rush this.

steps.text: Grill or sear the chicken until browned; set aside.
Caramelise all onions in oil until soft and golden, then add marinade juices and stock.
Return chicken and simmer until cooked through and the sauce is silky.

name: Fataya
adaptationNote: Fill with spiced lentils instead of fish for a vegetarian version — same crispy pastry, hearty inside.
blurb: Crisp half-moon pastries stuffed with spiced fish or meat — the snack of Dakar street stalls and Ramadan evenings. Best hot, with lime.

ingredients.name: Tinned sardines, drained
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Beef is milder; lentils make it vegetarian and still hearty.

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet, minced
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Easier to dose; same warmth.

steps.text: Mix flour, salt, oil and water into a soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
steps.why: Resting relaxes the dough so it rolls thin without springing back.

steps.text: Mash filling with onion, parsley, chilli and seasoning.
Roll, cut rounds, fill, fold and crimp edges well.
steps.why: Seal firmly or they burst open in the hot oil.

steps.text: Fry in batches until crisp and golden; drain on paper.

name: Akara
adaptationNote: Naturally vegan and gluten-free — just keep the frying oil fresh and hot.
blurb: Crisp black-eyed-bean fritters with a fluffy middle — Saturday-morning royalty with pap (ogi), and a party small-chop favourite.

ingredients.name: Dried black-eyed beans, soaked & peeled
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Skips the peeling labour; same result.

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Same warmth, easier to control.

steps.text: Blend soaked peeled beans with onion and pepper into a thick, fluffy batter — barely any water.
steps.why: Too much water makes them soak up oil and fall apart; thick batter fries crisp.

steps.text: Whisk in salt and rest 5 minutes.
Scoop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, turning, until deep golden.

name: Efo Riro
adaptationNote: Swap assorted meat and smoked fish for mushrooms to make this vegetarian — keep the palm oil and locust beans for depth.
blurb: A rich Yoruba spinach stew with palm oil, peppers and assorted meats — glossy, deeply savoury, and made for pounded yam.

ingredients.name: Fresh spinach
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Softer texture; squeeze very dry or the stew waters out.

ingredients.name: Palm oil
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Loses signature colour and earthiness — honest downgrade.

ingredients.name: Locust beans (iru)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Different but similarly deep and savoury.

ingredients.name: Assorted meat + smoked fish
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Lighter; keep palm oil and iru for the soul of the dish.

steps.text: Boil meats until tender; reserve stock. Blanch spinach, squeeze dry, chop roughly.
steps.why: Dry greens keep the stew glossy instead of watery.

steps.text: Fry pepper mix in palm oil until the oil floats and the sourness cooks off.
Add meats, fish, iru and a splash of stock; simmer to marry.
Fold in spinach and simmer briefly until just wilted and glossy.
steps.why: Greens go in last so they stay bright, not grey.

name: Pounded Yam
adaptationNote: Naturally vegan — pair with a vegetarian soup like mushroom efo riro.
blurb: The king of swallows — smooth, stretchy pounded yam, the proud partner of egusi and efo riro at celebrations and Sunday tables.

ingredients.name: White yam (puna), peeled & cubed
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Close and much quicker; slightly less stretch, still smooth.

steps.text: Boil yam in salted water until very tender — a knife slides through easily.
Pound (or beat with a stand mixer) adding splashes of hot water until completely smooth and stretchy.
steps.why: Lumps are the enemy — keep going until it pulls like dough.

steps.text: Mould into balls with wet hands and serve hot with soup.

name: Banku
adaptationNote: Naturally vegan — serve with vegetarian groundnut stew or okra.
blurb: Ghana's tangy fermented corn-and-cassava dough balls — soft, stretchy and made for tilapia, okra stew or groundnut soup.

ingredients.name: Fermented corn dough
ingredients.substitution: Fine cornmeal + 1 tbsp vinegar, rested 1 hour
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Milder tang; close enough for a first try.

ingredients.name: Cassava dough
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less stretch, still soft and tasty.

steps.text: Mix doughs with salted water into a smooth, thick paste.
Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly, until it pulls from the pot and turns translucent.
steps.why: Constant stirring is the whole trick — stop and it goes lumpy.

steps.text: Shape into balls and rest covered 5 minutes before serving.

name: Kelewele
adaptationNote: Naturally vegan — a great starter or party snack on its own.
blurb: Spicy fried plantain cubes tossed with ginger and chilli — Accra's famous night-market snack, crisp outside and caramel-sweet inside.

ingredients.name: Ripe (spotted) plantains
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Much softer and sweeter — fry briefly, honest downgrade.

ingredients.name: Grated ginger
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less fiery freshness, still warm.

steps.text: Cube plantain and toss with ginger, spices and salt. Rest 10 minutes.
steps.why: Resting lets the spice coat every cube instead of sliding off in the oil.

steps.text: Fry in hot oil until deep golden and caramelised at the edges.
Drain on paper and serve hot, with roasted peanuts if you like.
